title: How plants sense light
examples: What is phototropism and how does it work?
Does auxin only affect roots or shoots?
Why do plants bend towards the sunlight?

explain.say: Today we are learning how plants react to light.
One key process is called phototropism.
The plant hormone responsible is auxin.
Auxin moves to the shaded side of the shoot.
This uneven distribution causes the shoot to bend towards the light.
In real life, this helps seedlings reach sunlight for energy.

faq.q: What is the main purpose of phototropism?
faq.a: The main purpose is to help the plant grow towards a light source. This ensures the plant can photosynthesize efficiently for energy.
asks: Why do plants bend towards light?
Does light tell the plant where to grow?

faq.q: Is auxin the only hormone involved in this process?
faq.a: While auxin is the main hormone studied for this, other plant hormones can affect growth patterns. However, auxin is key to phototropism.
asks: Does auxin do everything in the plant?

faq.q: Does the concentration of auxin matter?
faq.a: Yes, the uneven concentration is important. More auxin on one side causes faster growth there, leading to the bend.
asks: Is the amount of auxin important?
What happens if auxin is too much?

faq.q: Does this process happen in all plants?
faq.a: Yes, phototropism is a common growth response seen in many types of plants. It is a fundamental survival mechanism.
asks: Is it a universal plant trait?

faq.q: What happens if the light source is removed?
faq.a: If the light source is removed, the plant will continue to grow, but the strong directional bending will stop. It will grow more randomly.
asks: What if there is no light?
Does it stop growing in the dark?
How does it grow without light?

facts: Phototropism is the directional growth of a plant in response to light.
Auxin is a plant hormone that controls cell elongation and growth.
When light hits one side, auxin moves to the shaded side.
Higher auxin concentration on one side promotes faster cell growth there.

quiz.say: A plant stem bends towards a window. This bending is an example of:
quiz.why: Phototropism is the specific term for growth in response to light.

wrong.0: Tropic is a general term for directional growth, but phototropism is the specific name for light response.
wrong.1: Photolysis is the splitting of molecules by light, which is a chemical process, not a growth direction.
wrong.2: Auxin is the chemical substance causing the effect, but phototropism names the overall biological process.

quiz.say: If auxin moves to the shaded side, what happens to the growth rate there?
quiz.why: Higher concentrations of auxin promote faster cell elongation on the shaded side.

wrong.0: Stopping growth would prevent the plant from reaching light.
wrong.1: Decreased growth would cause the plant to bend away from the light.
wrong.2: If the rate stayed the same, there would be no bending towards the light.

quiz.say: A student draws a diagram showing auxin moving from the light side to the dark side of a stem. What does this demonstrate?
quiz.why: The movement of auxin creating a gradient that causes bending is the definition of phototropism.

wrong.0: Geotropism is an older term often used interchangeably but phototropism is more specific to light.
wrong.2: Gravitropism is the response to gravity, not light.
wrong.3: Hydrotropism is the response to water, not light.
